Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old woman with 2-day history of worsening lower abdominal pain, pink urine, and mild systemic symptoms; empiric treatment for presumed urinary tract infection initiated.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Gradual onset burning pain below umbilicus for 2 days, worsening, constant.
- Associated symptoms: ↑ urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine, mild nausea, feeling hot/sweaty. No dysuria, no vomiting, no diarrhea, constipation has resolved. No respiratory, cardiac, neurologic complaints.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior similar episodes, no radiation of pain, no fever measured.
- Gynecologic/Sexual: Sexually active with one partner; last intercourse 4 days ago; Implanon in situ ×1 year; last period 2 weeks ago; last STI screen 6 months ago (normal). Pregnancy considered possible though unlikely.
- Past medical/surgical history: None significant; no surgeries.
- Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon). No other routine meds.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social: Accountant; lives with two roommates; non-smoker; social alcohol use.

Examination:
- (Telehealth visit – no physical examination performed.)
- Vitals: Not obtained.

Impression:
- Likely uncomplicated urinary tract infection; differentials include gastrointestinal cause or early pregnancy (pregnancy status unconfirmed).

Plan:
- Empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (route not documented); e-script sent to pharmacy.
- Symptomatic care: Paracetamol for pain; maintain adequate oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.
- Diagnostics: Home pregnancy test recommended to exclude pregnancy.
- Safety net: Return/seek care if pain worsens, fever develops, vomiting, or no improvement within a few days.
- Follow-up: Contact clinic in several days if symptoms persist or worsen.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements:
  - Drug allergies not elicited.
  - Current medication list may be incomplete beyond Implanon.
  - No objective vitals or abdominal/urinalysis findings (telehealth limitation).

● Internal transcript conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational fillers, no significant inaudible sections.
